title: How to Hide Your Baby From the Government
gist: WIRED profiles the 'sovereign baby' movement, an influencer-driven, digitally native outgrowth of sovereign citizen ideology in which US parents skip birth certificates and Social Security numbers and instead buy guides ($44-$5,555) to obtain passports via secondary evidence. Lawyers report rising cases since Covid, linked to homeschooling, free birth and distrust of government and medicine, while an adult raised undocumented describes lifelong harm.

insights.claim: Utah influencer Kristin LaHargoue's brand Veda Revival sells a $497 bundle of videos and templates for obtaining children's passports based on 'nationality' rather than 'citizenship', plus $997 personal 'hand-holding', and claims to have worked with over 1,000 parents.
insights.speaker: Paula Mejia
insights.so_what: Shows an unregulated creator-economy niche monetizing anti-government distrust at premium price points.

insights.claim: LaHargoue runs an affiliate program paying 15 to 20 percent commission for selling her sovereign baby services, and other influencers such as Minister Dionne (125,000 Instagram followers) sell 'Status Correction FastTrack Bundles' for up to $555.
insights.speaker: Paula Mejia
insights.so_what: Affiliate structures enable viral, MLM-like spread of fringe services across social platforms.

insights.claim: The 'straw man theory' central to sovereign ideology falsely holds that birth certificates open a government account that uses the child as human capital to back US debt after the 1930s abandonment of the gold standard; no US court has ever sided with these arguments.

insights.so_what: Documentation gaps compound across generations, imposing lasting administrative and economic costs.
